vi.L: Mọi sự ban tặng tốt lành và mọi món quà trọn vẹn đều từ trên cao, từ Cha của các vì sáng mà xuống; nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không có sự thay đổi, cũng không có bóng của sự xoay vần.
vi.B: Mọi sự ban tặng tốt lành và mọi món quà trọn vẹn đều từ trên cao. Những điều ấy đến từ Cha của các vì sáng trên bầu trời; nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không có sự thay đổi, cũng không có bóng nào do xoay chuyển mà ra.
vi.R: Mọi món quà tốt lành và trọn vẹn đều đến từ trời. Những món quà ấy đến từ Đức Chúa Trời là Cha, Đấng đã dựng nên mặt trời, mặt trăng và các ngôi sao. Ánh sáng của chúng di chuyển và thay đổi, bóng của chúng cũng đổi dời, nhưng Đức Chúa Trời không bao giờ thay đổi.

decisions.choice: every good giving and every perfect gift: the subject of the sentence
alternatives: every giving is good, and every perfect gift is from above
decisions.reason: The words most naturally form one subject: all good giving comes from above. The opening words of the verse happen to form a line of Greek verse, so James may be using a saying his readers knew.

decisions.choice: the Father of the lights: God, creator of the sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: God made the lights of the sky (Genesis 1:14-18; Psalm 136:7-9). Calling him their Father shows him as the source of light and of every good thing.

decisions.choice: no variation or shadow of turning: God does not change as the heavenly lights do
decisions.reason: τροπή can mean the turning of the heavenly bodies, and παραλλαγή change or variation. Sun and moon move, wax and wane, and cast moving shadows; God is not like them (Malachi 3:6).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "shadow of turning"
alternatives: "variation that belongs to the turning of a shadow"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts have a slightly different ending here, which makes the last words mean something like "the variation that comes with the turning of a shadow". The sense, that God does not change, is the same. This description is from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the lights in the sky
decisions.reason: Balanced says which lights are meant.

decisions.choice: God the Father, who made the sun, the moon, and the stars. Their light moves and changes...
alternatives: the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture: God made the heavenly lights, and unlike them he does not change.

decisions.choice: mianga
decisions.reason: "Nuru" is light itself, the word kept for light as a figure. James means the heavenly bodies that give light (see the meaning decision), which Swahili calls "mianga"; Balanced adds "ya angani", as the English Balanced adds "in the sky".

decisions.choice: "các vì sáng" for the lights
decisions.reason: The lights are the sun, moon and stars, which God made (m2). "Các vì sáng" is the Vietnamese way of naming the heavenly bodies as lights; "ánh sáng" would be light itself.

source.text: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας, εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων.

records.literal_gloss: Having willed he gave birth to us by word of truth, for the to be us firstfruits a certain of the of him creatures.

en.L: Having willed [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave birth to us by [the] word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} creatures.
en.B: It was {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will to give us birth through the word of truth, so that we might be something like the firstfruits among all {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has created.
en.R: God chose to give us new life through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} message of truth. He wanted us to be like the first part of the harvest, which belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the first of everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made.

es.L: Habiéndolo querido, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos hizo nacer por [la] palabra de verdad, para que seamos una especie de primicias de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} criaturas.
es.B: Fue {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad hacernos nacer por medio de la palabra de verdad, para que fuéramos algo así como las primicias de todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha creado.
es.R: Dios quiso darnos vida nueva por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mensaje de verdad. Quería que fuéramos como la primera parte de la cosecha, que le pertenece a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: lo primero de todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha hecho.

sw.L: Kwa kuwa alipenda [hivyo], alituzaa kupitia neno la kweli, ili tuwe aina fulani ya limbuko la viumbe {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}}.
sw.B: Ilikuwa ni mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kutuzaa kupitia neno la kweli, ili tuwe kitu kama limbuko miongoni mwa viumbe {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}} vyote.
sw.R: Mungu aliamua kutupa uzima mpya kupitia ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kweli. Alitaka tuwe kama sehemu ya kwanza ya mavuno, ambayo ni mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: wa kwanza kati ya vitu vyote alivyoviumba.

fr.L: Ayant voulu [cela], {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a mis au monde par [la] parole de vérité, pour que nous soyons comme des prémices de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} créatures.
fr.B: C’est par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} volonté qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a donné naissance par la parole de vérité, pour que nous soyons en quelque sorte les prémices de tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a créé.
fr.R: Dieu a choisi de nous donner une vie nouvelle par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} message de vérité. Il voulait que nous soyons comme la première partie de la récolte, celle qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartient : les premiers de tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait.

ko.L: [그분은] 뜻을 정하시고 진리의 말씀으로 우리를 낳으셨습니다. 우리가 그분이 지으신 것들 가운데 일종의 첫 열매가 되게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 하나님께서는 뜻하셔서 진리의 말씀으로 우리를 낳으셨습니다. 우리가 그분이 지으신 모든 것 가운데 첫 열매와 같은 사람들이 되게 하시려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 진리의 말씀을 통해 우리에게 새 생명을 주시기로 하셨습니다. 하나님께서는 우리가 추수할 때 맨 먼저 거두는 열매처럼 되기를 원하셨습니다. 그 첫 열매는 하나님의 것이고, 하나님께서 만드신 모든 것 가운데 처음입니다.

vi.L: Vì đã muốn [như vậy], {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sinh hạ chúng ta bởi lời của chân lý, để chúng ta trở nên một thứ trái đầu mùa trong các tạo vật của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã muốn sinh chúng ta ra bởi lời chân lý, để chúng ta trở nên như trái đầu mùa giữa mọi loài {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã dựng nên.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn ban cho chúng ta sự sống mới qua sứ điệp chân lý của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài muốn chúng ta giống như phần đầu tiên của mùa gặt, là phần thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, phần đầu tiên trong mọi vật {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã dựng nên.

decisions.choice: gave birth to us: God gave believers new life
decisions.reason: ἀποκυέω is the birth-verb of verse 15, now used of God: against sin's birth of death stands God's birth of a new people by his word (1 Peter 1:23). "Us" and "firstfruits" point to believers as the start of God's new creation, though some read it as God's first creation of humankind.

decisions.choice: having willed: by his own free choice
decisions.reason: βουληθεὶς stands first for emphasis. God's new birth comes from his own will, in contrast with the desire that gives birth to sin (verses 14-15).

decisions.choice: the word of truth: the message of the gospel
decisions.reason: The same phrase names the gospel in Colossians 1:5 and Ephesians 1:13. Verse 21 calls it "the implanted word".

decisions.choice: firstfruits: the first part of the harvest, given to God as a pledge of the rest
decisions.reason: Israel brought the first of each harvest to God (Exodus 23:19; Deuteronomy 26:1-11). Believers are the first share of what God will do for all his creation (Romans 8:19-23).

decisions.choice: God; new life; the first part of the harvest, which belongs to him
alternatives: he gave birth to us; firstfruits
decisions.reason: Readable names God, says what kind of birth this is, and explains "firstfruits".

decisions.choice: met au monde (1:15), nous a mis au monde (1:18) at Literal; donne naissance, nous a donné naissance at Balanced
decisions.reason: James uses the same verb for sin giving birth to death and for God giving birth to his people (m3 on 1:15). Literal and Balanced use the same French verb in both verses so the contrast can be heard.

decisions.choice: "낳으셨습니다" (L, B), the same verb as "죽음을 낳습니다" in verse 15; "새 생명을 주시다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision points out that James uses the verb of verse 15 here: sin gives birth to death, but God gives birth to us. Literal and Balanced keep the one Korean verb "낳다" so the contrast is heard; Readable says what the birth is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "진리" for truth at every level (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "진리" is the key term for truth in the Korean of John and Colossians; "참" is kept for the adjective.

decisions.choice: "trái đầu mùa" (L, B); "phần đầu tiên của mùa gặt" (R)
decisions.reason: Firstfruits are the first part of the harvest, given to God as a pledge of the rest (m4). "Trái đầu mùa" is the Vietnamese church phrase; Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Ἴστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί.

records.literal_gloss: Know [this], brothers of me beloved.

en.L: Know [this], my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: Be sure of this, my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.R: My dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, remember this.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sepan|Sabed}} [esto], hermanos míos amados.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} por seguro esto, mis queridos hermanos.
es.R: Mis queridos hermanos, {{plural_you:recuerden|recordad}} esto.

sw.L: Jueni [hili], ndugu zangu wapendwa.
sw.B: Fahamuni hili kwa hakika, ndugu zangu wapendwa.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu wapendwa, kumbukeni jambo hili.

fr.L: Sachez [cela], mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} bien-aimés.
fr.B: Soyez-en sûrs, mes chers {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.R: Mes chers {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, retenez bien ceci.

ko.L: [이것을] 아십시오, 사랑하는 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분.
ko.B: 사랑하는 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 이것을 꼭 알아 두십시오.
ko.R: 사랑하는 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 이것을 기억하십시오.

vi.L: Hãy biết [điều này], thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} yêu dấu của tôi.
vi.B: Hãy nắm chắc điều này, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} yêu dấu của tôi.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} yêu dấu của tôi, hãy nhớ điều này.

decisions.choice: know this: a command
alternatives: "you know [this]", a statement about what they already know
decisions.reason: Ἴστε can be a command or a statement; the forms are the same. As a command it calls attention to what follows; as a statement it points back to what God has done (verse 18).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "know"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read a different word meaning "so then", which joins this verse to verse 18; the oldest manuscripts read "know". This description is from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James speaks to the whole church, men and women, so the gender setting applies; the traditional "brothers" is the alternative. ἀγαπητοί is "loved": "my dear" says it in everyday words.

source.text: ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι, βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν, ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην θεοῦ οὐκ ἐργάζεται.

records.literal_gloss: And let be every man swift to the hearing, slow to the speaking, slow to anger; \v 20 for anger of man righteousness of God not works.

en.L: And let {{gender:every person|every man}} be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger; \v 20 for {{gender:a person's|a man's}} anger does not work [the] righteousness of God.
en.B: Every person should be eager to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger, \v 20 for {{gender:human anger|a man's anger}} does not accomplish the righteousness of God.
en.R: Everyone should be quick to listen and slow to speak. Do not be quick to get angry. \v 20 When people are angry, they do not live the righteous life that God wants.

es.L: Y que {{gender:todo ser humano|todo hombre}} sea pronto para oír, lento para hablar, lento para [la] ira; \v 20 porque la ira {{gender:del ser humano|del hombre}} no obra [la] justicia de Dios.
es.B: Toda persona debe estar dispuesta a escuchar, ser lenta para hablar y lenta para enojarse, \v 20 porque la ira {{gender:humana|del hombre}} no produce la justicia de Dios.
es.R: Todos deben estar listos para escuchar y ser lentos para hablar. No {{plural_you:se enojen|os enfadéis}} enseguida. \v 20 Cuando la gente se enoja, no vive la vida justa que Dios quiere.

sw.L: Na kila mwanadamu na awe mwepesi katika kusikia, mzito katika kusema, mzito katika kukasirika; \v 20 kwa maana hasira ya mtu haitendi haki ya Mungu.
sw.B: Kila mtu anapaswa kuwa tayari kusikiliza, kuchelewa kusema, na kuchelewa kukasirika, \v 20 kwa sababu hasira ya mwanadamu haitimizi haki ya Mungu.
sw.R: Kila mtu awe tayari kusikiliza na asiwe na haraka ya kusema. Msiwe wepesi wa kukasirika. \v 20 Watu wanapokasirika, hawaishi maisha ya haki ambayo Mungu anataka.

fr.L: Que {{gender:tout être humain|tout homme}} soit prompt à écouter, lent à parler, lent à la colère ; \v 20 car la colère de l’{{gender:être humain|homme}} n’accomplit pas la justice de Dieu.
fr.B: Chacun doit être prompt à écouter, lent à parler et lent à se mettre en colère, \v 20 car la colère {{gender:humaine|de l’homme}} ne produit pas la justice que Dieu demande.
fr.R: Chacun doit être prêt à écouter et lent à parler. Ne vous mettez pas vite en colère. \v 20 Quand les gens se mettent en colère, ils ne vivent pas de la manière juste que Dieu veut.

ko.L: 사람은 누구나 듣기는 빨리 하고, 말하기는 더디 하고, 화내기도 더디 해야 합니다. \v 20 사람의 화는 하나님의 의를 이루지 못하기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 누구나 듣기는 빨리 하고, 말하기는 더디 하고, 화내기도 더디 하십시오. \v 20 사람의 화는 하나님의 의를 이루지 못합니다.
ko.R: 누구나 남의 말을 잘 듣고, 말은 천천히 하십시오. 쉽게 화내지 마십시오. \v 20 사람이 화를 낼 때에는 하나님께서 원하시는 의로운 삶을 살지 못합니다.

vi.L: Nhưng mọi người hãy mau nghe, chậm nói, chậm giận; \v 20 vì cơn giận của con người không làm nên sự công chính của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Mỗi người phải mau lắng nghe, chậm nói và chậm giận, \v 20 vì cơn giận của con người không thực hiện được sự công chính của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Mọi người nên mau lắng nghe và chậm nói. Đừng vội nổi giận. \v 20 Khi người ta nổi giận, họ không sống đời sống công chính mà Đức Chúa Trời muốn.

decisions.choice: the righteousness of God: the right conduct God requires and approves
alternatives: God's justice, which human anger thinks it is carrying out
decisions.reason: James is speaking about how believers live: anger does not produce the life God counts right. The phrase can also mean God's own justice, which no angry person brings about on God's behalf.

decisions.choice: anger: settled human anger, quick temper
decisions.reason: ὀργή is the anger of the person "slow to anger" in verse 19; the wisdom books warn against it (Proverbs 14:29; Ecclesiastes 7:9).

decisions.choice: quick to hear, slow to speak: Israel's wisdom
decisions.reason: Proverbs says the same: the many words of a fool (Proverbs 10:19; 29:20) and the soft answer that turns away wrath (Proverbs 15:1).

decisions.choice: every person; a man: anyone at all
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος is the general word for a human being; ἀνήρ usually means a man, but in James's sayings it stands for anyone (1:8, 1:12).

decisions.choice: {{gender:every person|every man}}; {{gender:a person's|a man's}}
decisions.reason: The sayings are for everyone, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: they do not live the righteous life that God wants
alternatives: does not produce the righteousness of God
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of righteousness is meant (see the theology decision).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:se enojen|os enfadéis}}
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the readers, as the English Readable does. The setting also uses each region's everyday verb: "enojarse" in Latin America, "enfadarse" in Spain.

decisions.choice: hasira, kukasirika
decisions.reason: This is human anger, so Swahili says "hasira"; "ghadhabu" is kept for the wrath of God, as in Romans.

decisions.choice: {{gender:tout être humain|tout homme}}, l’{{gender:être humain|homme}} (L); Chacun, la colère {{gender:humaine|de l’homme}} (B)
decisions.reason: Both words mean anyone at all (m4). As in Colossians, "tout être humain" agrees like "tout homme", so only the noun changes; Balanced says "chacun", which is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: la justice (L, B); de la manière juste (R)
decisions.reason: "Justice" is the key term for righteousness at every level in Hebrews; here it is the right conduct God requires (m1), which Readable says plainly while keeping "juste".

decisions.choice: "하나님의 의" (L, B); "하나님께서 원하시는 의로운 삶" (R) (for the whole letter: "의" for righteousness, "의로운 사람" for the righteous)
decisions.reason: "의" is the key term the Korean style guide gives for righteousness, as in the Korean of Romans. The meaning decision reads it here as the right conduct God requires, so Readable keeps the root in "의로운" and says what it is.

decisions.choice: "sự công chính" for righteousness (L, B); "đời sống công chính" (R), through the letter
decisions.reason: "Sự công chính" is the key term of the Vietnamese style guide, used in John and Romans. Here it is the right conduct God requires (m1), which Readable says plainly, as the English Readable does. "Mọi người" and "con người" need no gender span.

source.text: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore having put off all filthiness and excess of wickedness in gentleness receive the implanted word the [one] being able to save the souls of you.

en.L: Therefore, having put off all filthiness and [the] excess of wickedness, in gentleness receive the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
en.B: So take off all that is filthy and the wickedness that overflows, and with a gentle spirit welcome the word rooted in you, which has the power to save your souls.
en.R: So get rid of everything dirty and evil in your lives. Be humble, and welcome the message that God has planted in your hearts. It has the power to save you.

es.L: Por tanto, quitándo{{plural_you:se|os}} toda suciedad y [la] abundancia de maldad, {{plural_you:reciban|recibid}} con mansedumbre la palabra plantada, la que puede salvar {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} almas.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:quítense|quitaos}} todo lo sucio y la maldad que se desborda, y con un espíritu manso {{plural_you:acojan|acoged}} la palabra plantada en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que tiene poder para salvar {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} almas.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} todo lo sucio y malo que hay en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida. {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} humildes y {{plural_you:reciban|recibid}} el mensaje que Dios ha plantado en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón. Ese mensaje tiene poder para {{plural_you:salvarlos|salvaros}}.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo, mkishavua kila uchafu na wingi wa uovu, karibisheni kwa upole neno lililopandwa [ndani yenu], lenye uwezo wa kuokoa nafsi zenu.
sw.B: Basi vueni kila kitu kichafu na uovu unaofurika, na kwa roho ya upole mlipokee neno lililopandwa ndani yenu, ambalo lina nguvu ya kuokoa nafsi zenu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo achaneni na kila kitu kichafu na kiovu maishani mwenu. Muwe wanyenyekevu, mkaukaribishe ujumbe ambao Mungu ameupanda mioyoni mwenu. Ujumbe huo una nguvu ya kuwaokoa.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, vous étant débarrassés de toute saleté et de [tout] excès de méchanceté, recevez avec douceur la parole implantée, qui peut sauver vos âmes.
fr.B: Débarrassez-vous donc de toute impureté et du mal qui déborde, et accueillez avec douceur la parole plantée en vous, qui a le pouvoir de sauver vos âmes.
fr.R: Alors, rejetez tout ce qui est sale et mauvais dans votre vie. Soyez humbles, et accueillez le message que Dieu a planté dans votre cœur. Il a le pouvoir de vous sauver.

ko.L: 그러므로 모든 더러움과 넘치는 악을 벗어 버리고, 여러분 안에 심어진 말씀을 온유함으로 받아들이십시오. 그 말씀은 여러분의 영혼을 구원할 수 있습니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 모든 더러운 것과 넘쳐 나는 악을 벗어 버리고, 여러분 안에 뿌리내린 말씀을 온유한 마음으로 받아들이십시오. 그 말씀에는 여러분의 영혼을 구원할 능력이 있습니다.
ko.R: 그러니 여러분의 삶에서 더럽고 악한 것을 모두 버리십시오. 겸손한 마음으로, 하나님께서 여러분 마음에 심어 주신 말씀을 받아들이십시오. 그 말씀은 여러분을 구원할 능력이 있습니다.

vi.L: Vậy, hãy cởi bỏ mọi sự dơ bẩn và sự gian ác tràn lan, và với lòng nhu mì tiếp nhận lời đã được gieo vào [lòng], là lời có thể cứu linh hồn anh chị em.
vi.B: Vậy hãy cởi bỏ mọi điều dơ bẩn và sự gian ác đang tràn lan, rồi với tinh thần nhu mì, hãy đón nhận lời đã được gieo vào lòng anh chị em, là lời có quyền năng cứu linh hồn anh chị em.
vi.R: Vậy hãy loại bỏ mọi điều dơ bẩn và gian ác trong đời sống mình. Hãy khiêm nhường đón nhận sứ điệp mà Đức Chúa Trời đã gieo vào lòng anh chị em. Sứ điệp ấy có quyền năng cứu anh chị em.

decisions.choice: put off: as one takes off dirty clothes
decisions.reason: ἀποτίθημι is used for taking off clothing, and the New Testament uses it for leaving behind the old way of life (Colossians 3:8; Ephesians 4:22). "Filthiness" is the word for dirty clothes in 2:2.

decisions.choice: excess of wickedness: the evil that overflows
alternatives: what is left over of wickedness
decisions.reason: περισσεία means abundance or surplus. It describes wickedness that spills over, especially in angry words (verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: implanted: planted within by God
decisions.reason: ἔμφυτος can mean inborn, but here the word is received, so it has been planted from outside. It is the word of truth of verse 18, and recalls God's promise to put his law within his people (Jeremiah 31:33).

decisions.choice: souls: the whole person, saved at the last day
decisions.reason: ψυχή here is the person as a whole, before God. The salvation in view is final rescue from death and judgment, as in 5:20.

decisions.choice: save you
decisions.reason: Readable says "you", since "soul" here means the whole person (see the meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep "souls".

decisions.choice: with a gentle spirit
decisions.reason: πραΰτης is the gentleness that stands against anger (verse 20); "meekness" is no longer everyday English.

decisions.choice: kuvua
decisions.reason: "Kuvua" is the verb for taking off clothes, which keeps the picture of the meaning decision (dirty clothes put off). Readable says plainly "achaneni na".

decisions.choice: "영혼" (L, B); "여러분" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "souls" as the whole person saved at the last day. "목숨" (the style guide's word for this noun in John) would mean physical life here; "영혼" is the ordinary Korean for the self that God saves. Readable says "you", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "cởi bỏ" (L, B) for put off
decisions.reason: The verb pictures taking off dirty clothes (m1); "cởi bỏ" keeps the picture, as the Vietnamese Colossians does (3:8). Readable says plainly "loại bỏ".

source.text: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And become doers of word and not hearers only deceiving yourselves.

en.L: And become doers of [the] word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
en.B: Be people who carry out the word, not just people who hear it. Otherwise you are fooling yourselves.
en.R: Hearing God's message is not enough. You must also do what it says, or you are only tricking yourselves.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:sean|sed}} hacedores de [la] palabra y no solamente oidores, {{plural_you:engañándose a sí mismos|engañándoos a vosotros mismos}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} personas que ponen por obra la palabra, no solo que la oyen. De lo contrario, {{plural_you:se engañan a sí mismos|os engañáis a vosotros mismos}}.
es.R: No basta con oír el mensaje de Dios. También {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que hacer lo que dice, o solo {{plural_you:se están engañando|os estáis engañando}} a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos.

sw.L: Na iweni watendaji wa neno, si wasikilizaji peke yake, mkijidanganya wenyewe.
sw.B: Muwe watu wanaolitekeleza neno, si watu wanaolisikia tu. La sivyo mnajidanganya wenyewe.
sw.R: Kusikia ujumbe wa Mungu hakutoshi. Ni lazima pia mfanye unavyosema, la sivyo mnajidanganya tu.

fr.L: Et devenez des gens qui pratiquent [la] parole, et non des auditeurs seulement, vous trompant vous-mêmes.
fr.B: Mettez la parole en pratique, au lieu de vous contenter de l’écouter : ce serait vous tromper vous-mêmes.
fr.R: Écouter le message de Dieu ne suffit pas. Vous devez aussi faire ce qu’il dit, sinon vous vous trompez vous-mêmes.

ko.L: 그리고 말씀을 행하는 사람이 되고, 듣기만 하여 자기 자신을 속이는 사람이 되지 마십시오.
ko.B: 말씀을 듣기만 하는 사람이 되지 말고 실천하는 사람이 되십시오. 그렇지 않으면 여러분은 자신을 속이는 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님의 말씀을 듣는 것만으로는 충분하지 않습니다. 말씀대로 행해야 합니다. 그렇지 않으면 여러분은 자기 자신을 속이고 있을 뿐입니다.

vi.L: Và hãy trở nên những người làm theo lời, chứ không chỉ là những người nghe mà thôi, tự lừa dối chính mình.
vi.B: Hãy là những người làm theo lời, chứ không chỉ nghe lời mà thôi; nếu không, anh chị em đang tự lừa dối mình.
vi.R: Nghe sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời thôi thì chưa đủ. Anh chị em còn phải làm theo điều sứ điệp ấy dạy, nếu không thì anh chị em chỉ đang tự lừa mình mà thôi.

decisions.choice: doers: people whose lives carry out what they hear
decisions.reason: ποιητής is one who does. Paul makes the same point: not the hearers of the law but the doers are right with God (Romans 2:13). Jesus ends the Sermon on the Mount with it (Matthew 7:24-27).

decisions.choice: hearers: Scripture was mostly heard, read aloud in the gathering
decisions.reason: Few people owned books; the word was heard in synagogue and church. A "hearer" was a member of the listening congregation.

decisions.choice: deceiving yourselves: reasoning yourselves into a false belief
decisions.reason: παραλογίζομαι means to deceive by false reasoning: thinking that hearing is enough.

decisions.choice: people who carry out the word; people who hear it
decisions.reason: "Doers" and "hearers" are not natural English nouns; Balanced says the same with "people who". Literal keeps the nouns.

decisions.choice: des gens qui pratiquent [la] parole (L), also "ne la pratique pas" (1:23) and "quelqu’un qui pratique" (1:25)
decisions.reason: French has no current noun for "doer": "faiseur" is pejorative and "pratiquant" means someone who keeps up religious observance. Literal uses the verb "pratiquer" each time the noun occurs, and keeps the noun "auditeur" beside it.

decisions.choice: "행하는 사람" (L); "실천하는 사람" (B); "듣는 사람" for the hearer, through verse 25
decisions.reason: Korean has no everyday nouns for "doer" and "hearer", so it says "the one who does" and "the one who hears". Balanced uses "실천하다", the common word for putting teaching into practice.

source.text: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής, οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ, κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν.

records.literal_gloss: Because if anyone a hearer of word is and not a doer, this one is like a man looking at the face of the birth of him in a mirror; \v 24 for he looked at himself and has gone away and immediately forgot of what sort he was.

en.L: For if anyone is a hearer of [the] word and not a doer, this [one] is like a man looking closely at his natural face in a mirror; \v 24 for he looked at himself and has gone away, and at once forgot what he was like.
en.B: Anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man studying his own face in a mirror. \v 24 He looks himself over, goes away, and at once forgets what he looked like.
en.R: Some people hear God's message but do not do what it says. They are like a man who looks at his face in a mirror. \v 24 He sees himself, then walks away, and soon he cannot remember what his face was like.

es.L: Porque si alguno es oidor de [la] palabra y no hacedor, este se parece a un hombre que observa atentamente su rostro natural en un espejo; \v 24 porque se observó a sí mismo y se ha ido, y enseguida olvidó cómo era.
es.B: Quien oye la palabra pero no la pone por obra es como un hombre que se mira detenidamente la cara en un espejo. \v 24 Se observa, se va, y enseguida olvida cómo era su aspecto.
es.R: Algunas personas oyen el mensaje de Dios, pero no hacen lo que dice. Son como un hombre que se mira la cara en un espejo. \v 24 Se ve, luego se va, y pronto ya no recuerda cómo era su cara.

sw.L: Kwa sababu mtu yeyote akiwa msikilizaji wa neno wala si mtendaji, huyo ni kama mtu anayeutazama kwa makini uso aliozaliwa nao katika kioo; \v 24 kwa maana alijiangalia, akaondoka, na papo hapo akasahau jinsi alivyokuwa.
sw.B: Mtu anayesikia neno lakini hatendi linavyosema ni kama mtu anayechunguza uso wake katika kioo. \v 24 Anajiangalia, anaondoka, na mara moja anasahau sura yake ilivyokuwa.
sw.R: Watu wengine husikia ujumbe wa Mungu lakini hawafanyi unavyosema. Wao ni kama mtu anayejiangalia uso katika kioo. \v 24 Anajiona, kisha anaondoka, na baada ya muda mfupi hakumbuki uso wake ulivyokuwa.

fr.L: Car si quelqu’un est auditeur de [la] parole et ne la pratique pas, celui-là ressemble à un homme qui observe dans un miroir le visage de sa naissance ; \v 24 car il s’est observé et s’en est allé, et aussitôt il a oublié comment il était.
fr.B: Celui qui écoute la parole sans la mettre en pratique ressemble à un homme qui examine son propre visage dans un miroir. \v 24 Il se regarde, il s’en va, et il oublie aussitôt de quoi il avait l’air.
fr.R: Certaines personnes écoutent le message de Dieu mais ne font pas ce qu’il dit. Elles sont comme un homme qui regarde son visage dans un miroir. \v 24 Il se voit, puis il s’en va, et bientôt il ne se rappelle plus à quoi ressemblait son visage.

ko.L: 누구든지 말씀을 듣기만 하고 행하지 않으면, 그는 거울로 자기의 타고난 얼굴을 자세히 보는 사람과 같습니다. \v 24 그는 자기를 보고 떠나가서, 곧 자기가 어떠했는지를 잊어버립니다.
ko.B: 말씀을 듣고도 행하지 않는 사람은 거울에 비친 자기 얼굴을 자세히 들여다보는 사람과 같습니다. \v 24 그는 자기 모습을 살펴보고 떠나가서는 곧 자기가 어떻게 생겼는지 잊어버립니다.
ko.R: 하나님의 말씀을 듣고도 그대로 하지 않는 사람들이 있습니다. 그들은 거울로 자기 얼굴을 보는 사람과 같습니다. \v 24 그는 자기 얼굴을 보고 나서 그 자리를 떠나면, 곧 자기 얼굴이 어떻게 생겼는지 기억하지 못합니다.

vi.L: Vì nếu ai là người nghe lời mà không phải là người làm theo, người ấy giống như một người đàn ông nhìn kỹ khuôn mặt bẩm sinh của mình trong gương; \v 24 vì anh ta đã nhìn chính mình rồi bỏ đi, và lập tức quên mất mình như thế nào.
vi.B: Ai nghe lời mà không làm theo thì giống như một người đàn ông chăm chú xem mặt mình trong gương. \v 24 Anh ta ngắm mình xong, bỏ đi, và lập tức quên mất mặt mình trông ra sao.
vi.R: Có những người nghe sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời nhưng không làm theo. Họ giống như một người đàn ông soi mặt mình trong gương. \v 24 Anh ta thấy mình, rồi bỏ đi, và chẳng bao lâu đã không nhớ mặt mình trông như thế nào.

decisions.choice: look at: observe carefully, not glance
decisions.reason: κατανοέω means to look attentively. The man does look carefully; the fault is that he walks away and forgets. Verse 25 sets against him the one who keeps looking.

decisions.choice: the face of his birth: his natural face, the face he was born with
alternatives: his true self, the person he really is
decisions.reason: "Of his birth" (γενέσεως) means the face he has by nature. Some see a hint of a person's true self, but the picture is first of all an ordinary face in a mirror.

decisions.choice: mirror: polished metal, giving a dim picture
decisions.reason: Mirrors were made of polished bronze or other metal (1 Corinthians 13:12).

decisions.choice: looked, has gone away, forgot: quick, vivid succession
decisions.reason: The verbs switch between past and perfect, which makes the little scene lively: a look, a departure, and the face is gone.

decisions.choice: a man
decisions.reason: ἀνήρ is "man". He is a figure in a picture, not a general statement about people, so no gender setting is used and the pronouns stay "he" and "his".

decisions.choice: mtu
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "man", and the English keeps "a man" because he is a figure in a picture. Swahili "mtu" (a person) tells the picture just as well, and "mwanamume" would stress that he is male, which is not the point.

decisions.choice: uso aliozaliwa nao
decisions.reason: "The face he was born with" keeps the Greek "of his birth" and means his natural face, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "타고난 얼굴" (L)
decisions.reason: "The face of his birth" is the face a person was born with (meaning decision); Korean "타고난" (born with) keeps the idiom at Literal, and Balanced and Readable say "자기 얼굴".

decisions.choice: "một người đàn ông", "anh ta" for the man at the mirror, with no gender span
decisions.reason: James's picture uses the word for a man, as the English keeps "a man"; Vietnamese names him as a man and gives him the everyday pronoun "anh ta".

source.text: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας, οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου, οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται.

records.literal_gloss: But the [one] having looked into law perfect the of the freedom and having stayed, not a hearer of forgetfulness having become but a doer of work, this one blessed in the doing of him will be.

en.L: But the one who has looked into [the] perfect law, the [law] of freedom, and has stayed [with it], having become not a hearer who forgets but a doer of [the] work, this [one] will be blessed in {{gender:their|his}} doing.
en.B: But whoever looks closely into the perfect law of freedom and stays with it, not hearing and then forgetting but doing the work, will be blessed in what {{gender:they do|he does}}.
en.R: But some people look closely into God's perfect law, the law of freedom, and they keep on looking. They do not forget what they hear. They do what it says. God will bless them in what they do.

es.L: Pero el que ha mirado atentamente en [la] ley perfecta, la de la libertad, y ha permanecido [en ella], no habiéndose hecho oidor olvidadizo sino hacedor de [la] obra, este será bienaventurado en su hacer.
es.B: Pero quien mira con atención la ley perfecta de la libertad y se queda en ella, no oyendo para luego olvidar, sino haciendo la obra, será bienaventurado en lo que hace.
es.R: Pero hay personas que miran con atención la ley perfecta de Dios, la ley que da libertad, y siguen mirándola. No olvidan lo que oyen. Hacen lo que dice. Dios las bendecirá en lo que hacen.

sw.L: Lakini yule aliyeinama kuchungulia katika sheria kamilifu, ile ya uhuru, na akaendelea [nayo], akiwa si msikilizaji anayesahau bali mtendaji wa kazi, huyo atakuwa heri katika utendaji wake.
sw.B: Lakini mtu anayechunguza kwa makini sheria kamilifu ya uhuru na kuendelea nayo, asiyesikia kisha akasahau bali anayetenda kazi inayotakiwa, atabarikiwa katika kile anachofanya.
sw.R: Lakini watu wengine huichunguza kwa makini sheria kamilifu ya Mungu, sheria inayoleta uhuru, nao huendelea kuitazama. Hawasahau wanachosikia. Wanafanya inavyosema. Mungu atawabariki katika yale wanayofanya.

fr.L: Mais celui qui s’est penché sur [la] loi parfaite, celle de la liberté, et qui [y] est resté, n’étant pas devenu un auditeur oublieux mais quelqu’un qui pratique l’œuvre, celui-là sera bienheureux dans ce qu’il fait.
fr.B: Mais celui qui plonge son regard dans la loi parfaite, la loi de la liberté, et qui s’y tient, sans écouter pour oublier ensuite mais en accomplissant l’œuvre, celui-là sera bienheureux dans ce qu’il fait.
fr.R: Mais d’autres regardent avec attention la loi parfaite de Dieu, la loi qui rend libre, et ils continuent à la regarder. Ils n’oublient pas ce qu’ils entendent. Ils font ce qu’elle dit. Dieu les bénira dans tout ce qu’ils font.

ko.L: 그러나 완전한 율법, 곧 자유의 [율법을] 들여다보고 [그 곁에] 머무는 사람은, 잊어버리는 듣는 사람이 아니라 일을 행하는 사람이 되어, 자기가 행하는 일에서 복을 받을 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 자유를 주는 완전한 율법을 자세히 들여다보고 그 곁을 떠나지 않는 사람, 곧 듣고 잊어버리는 사람이 아니라 실천하는 사람은 자기가 하는 일에서 복을 받을 것입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 하나님의 완전한 율법, 곧 자유를 주는 율법을 자세히 들여다보고, 계속해서 들여다보는 사람들이 있습니다. 그들은 들은 것을 잊어버리지 않고, 그 말씀대로 행합니다. 하나님께서는 그들이 하는 일에 복을 주실 것입니다.

vi.L: Nhưng người đã cúi xuống nhìn kỹ vào luật pháp trọn vẹn, là [luật pháp] của sự tự do, và đã ở lại [với luật ấy], không trở thành người nghe rồi quên, nhưng là người làm theo công việc, thì người ấy sẽ được phước trong việc mình làm.
vi.B: Nhưng ai chăm chú xem xét luật pháp trọn vẹn của sự tự do và cứ gắn bó với luật ấy, không nghe rồi quên nhưng thực hành điều mình nghe, thì người ấy sẽ được phước trong việc mình làm.
vi.R: Nhưng có những người chăm chú nhìn vào luật pháp trọn vẹn của Đức Chúa Trời, là luật pháp đem lại tự do, và họ cứ tiếp tục nhìn vào đó. Họ không quên điều mình nghe. Họ làm theo điều luật pháp ấy dạy. Đức Chúa Trời sẽ ban phước cho họ trong việc họ làm.

decisions.choice: looked into: bent down to look closely
decisions.reason: παρακύπτω is used of stooping to look into the empty tomb (John 20:5, 11) and of angels longing to look into the gospel (1 Peter 1:12). It is a close, intent look, and "stayed" says the person keeps looking.

decisions.choice: the perfect law of freedom: God's law as received and fulfilled in Jesus' teaching
alternatives: a principle of freedom with no commands
decisions.reason: The "law" is God's law, which James quotes in 2:8-11 and calls "the royal law". It is "perfect" (complete, Psalm 19:8) and "of freedom" because it is the word planted in the heart (verse 21), which sets people free rather than enslaving them (Psalm 119:45; John 8:31-32).

decisions.choice: a hearer of forgetfulness: a forgetful hearer
decisions.reason: The genitive describes the kind of hearer: one marked by forgetting, like the man at the mirror.

decisions.choice: will be blessed: in the doing itself, and at the end
decisions.reason: The future "will be" looks ahead to God's blessing, but "in his doing" places it in the very act of obeying (John 13:17).

decisions.choice: They do what it says
decisions.reason: ἔργον here is the doing the law asks for. Readable says it plainly instead of "work".

decisions.choice: God will bless them in what they do
alternatives: will be blessed in their doing
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who blesses.

decisions.choice: aliyeinama kuchungulia
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is stooping to look closely (see the meaning decision); Literal says "bent down to peer into". Balanced and Readable say "anachunguza kwa makini" (examines carefully).

decisions.choice: la loi parfaite, la loi de la liberté, lowercase (also 2:8, 2:12); la Loi, capitalised, where James speaks of the Law of Moses with its commandments (2:9-11; 4:11)
decisions.reason: The French style guide capitalises "la Loi" for the Law of Moses. Here James describes God’s law as he understands it, perfect and giving freedom (m2), and the description carries the meaning, so the common noun is used; where the commandments of Sinai are quoted and weighed, French writes "la Loi".

decisions.choice: "자유를 주는 율법" (B, R); "자유의 [율법]" (L)
decisions.reason: "The law of freedom" is God's law received through Jesus's teaching, which sets people free to obey (meaning decision). The bare genitive "자유의 율법" reads oddly in Korean, so Balanced and Readable say how law and freedom are related.

source.text: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone thinks religious to be not bridling tongue of him but deceiving heart of him, of this one worthless the religion.

en.L: If anyone thinks {{gender:they are|he is}} religious, not bridling {{gender:their|his}} tongue but deceiving {{gender:their|his}} heart, this person's religion is worthless.
en.B: If anyone thinks {{gender:they are|he is}} devout but does not put a bridle on {{gender:their|his}} tongue, {{gender:they are|he is}} fooling {{gender:themselves|himself}}, and {{gender:their|his}} religion is empty.
en.R: Some people think they serve God well, but they do not control what they say. They are fooling themselves, and their religion is worth nothing.

es.L: Si alguien cree ser religioso, sin refrenar su lengua sino engañando a su corazón, la religión de ese es vana.
es.B: Si alguien se cree piadoso, pero no le pone freno a su lengua, se engaña a sí mismo, y su religión está vacía.
es.R: Algunas personas creen que sirven bien a Dios, pero no controlan lo que dicen. Se engañan a sí mismas, y su religión no vale nada.

sw.L: Ikiwa mtu anajiona kuwa mtu wa dini, bila kuutia ulimi wake hatamu, bali akiudanganya moyo wake, dini ya huyo ni bure.
sw.B: Mtu akijiona kuwa mcha Mungu lakini hauwekei ulimi wake hatamu, anajidanganya mwenyewe, na dini yake ni tupu.
sw.R: Watu wengine hudhani kwamba wanamtumikia Mungu vizuri, lakini hawazuii maneno yao. Wanajidanganya wenyewe, na dini yao haina thamani yoyote.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un pense être religieux, ne tenant pas sa langue en bride mais trompant son cœur, la religion de celui-là est vaine.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un se croit pieux mais ne met pas de bride à sa langue, il se trompe lui-même, et sa religion est vide.
fr.R: Certains pensent qu’ils servent bien Dieu, mais ils ne contrôlent pas ce qu’ils disent. Ils se trompent eux-mêmes, et leur religion ne vaut rien.

ko.L: 누구든지 자기가 종교적이라고 생각하면서도 자기 혀에 재갈을 물리지 않고 자기 마음을 속이면, 이 사람의 종교는 헛된 것입니다.
ko.B: 누구든지 스스로 신앙생활을 잘한다고 생각하면서도 자기 혀에 재갈을 물리지 않는다면, 그는 자기를 속이는 것이고 그의 신앙생활은 헛된 것입니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람들은 자기가 하나님을 잘 섬긴다고 생각하지만, 자기가 하는 말을 다스리지 못합니다. 그들은 자기 자신을 속이고 있고, 그들의 신앙생활은 아무 쓸모가 없습니다.

vi.L: Nếu ai nghĩ mình là người sùng đạo, mà không kìm cương lưỡi mình, nhưng lừa dối lòng mình, thì sự sùng đạo của người ấy là vô ích.
vi.B: Nếu ai nghĩ mình sùng đạo mà không biết kìm cương lưỡi mình, thì người ấy đang tự lừa dối mình, và sự sùng đạo của người ấy là trống rỗng.
vi.R: Có người nghĩ rằng mình đang phụng sự Đức Chúa Trời cách tốt đẹp, nhưng lại không giữ gìn lời nói. Họ đang tự lừa dối mình, và việc giữ đạo của họ chẳng có giá trị gì.

decisions.choice: religious, religion: the outward practice of worship
decisions.reason: θρησκεία is the practice of religion: worship, prayer, keeping rituals (Acts 26:5). James does not reject it but asks what true practice looks like (verse 27).

decisions.choice: thinks: considers himself
decisions.reason: δοκέω can mean "seem" or "think". With "deceiving his heart" it is the person's own opinion of himself that is at fault.

decisions.choice: bridle the tongue: control speech as a rider controls a horse
decisions.reason: χαλιναγωγέω means to guide with a bridle. James develops the picture in 3:2-3.

decisions.choice: worthless: empty, achieving nothing
decisions.reason: μάταιος means futile; it is used of idols and empty ways (Acts 14:15; 1 Peter 1:18).

decisions.choice: fooling themselves
decisions.reason: "Heart" is the person within; Balanced and Readable say "themselves". Literal keeps "heart".

decisions.choice: kuutia ulimi hatamu
decisions.reason: "Hatamu" is a bridle, so Literal and Balanced keep James's picture of a rider controlling a horse, which he develops in 3:2-3. Readable says plainly "hawazuii maneno yao".

decisions.choice: "종교적이다 / 종교" (L); "신앙생활" (B, R), here and in verse 27
decisions.reason: The words mean the outward practice of worship (meaning decision). Literal keeps the plain "종교"; Balanced and Readable say "신앙생활", the everyday word for practising one's faith. "경건" is kept for the different word for godliness in 1 and 2 Peter, so the two do not blur.

decisions.choice: "sùng đạo", "sự sùng đạo" (L, B); "việc giữ đạo" (R) for religious, religion (also verse 27)
decisions.reason: The words mean the outward practice of worship (m1). "Tôn giáo" names a religion as a system or institution, which is not James's point; "sùng đạo" says a person devoted to the practice of faith, and Readable says "giữ đạo", keeping one's religious duties.

source.text: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν, ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν, ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: Religion pure and undefiled before the God and Father this is, to visit orphans and widows in the affliction of them, unstained oneself to keep from the world.

en.L: Religion pure and undefiled before [our] God and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, [and] to keep oneself unstained from the world.
en.B: To God the Father, religion that is pure and untainted looks like this: going to the help of orphans and widows in their trouble, and keeping yourself unstained by the world.
en.R: Here is the kind of religion that God the Father sees as pure and good: caring for orphans and widows when they are suffering, and not letting the world's evil make you dirty.

es.L: [La] religión pura e incontaminada delante del Dios y Padre es esta: visitar a [los] huérfanos y a [las] viudas en su aflicción, [y] guardarse a sí mismo sin mancha del mundo.
es.B: Para Dios el Padre, la religión pura y sin contaminación es esta: acudir en ayuda de los huérfanos y de las viudas en sus dificultades, y mantenerse sin mancha del mundo.
es.R: Esta es la religión que Dios el Padre considera pura y buena: cuidar a los huérfanos y a las viudas cuando sufren, y no dejarse ensuciar por la maldad del mundo.

sw.L: Dini safi isiyotiwa najisi mbele ya Mungu na Baba ni hii: kuwatembelea yatima na wajane katika taabu zao, [na] kujitunza bila doa kutokana na ulimwengu.
sw.B: Mbele ya Mungu Baba, dini iliyo safi na isiyochafuliwa ni hii: kuwasaidia yatima na wajane katika shida zao, na kujiweka mwenyewe bila doa la ulimwengu.
sw.R: Hii ndiyo dini ambayo Mungu Baba anaiona kuwa safi na njema: kuwatunza yatima na wajane wanapoteseka, na kujilinda usichafuliwe na uovu wa ulimwengu.

fr.L: [La] religion pure et sans souillure devant [notre] Dieu et Père est celle-ci : visiter les orphelins et les veuves dans leur détresse, [et] se garder sans tache loin du monde.
fr.B: Aux yeux de Dieu le Père, la religion pure et sans souillure consiste à venir en aide aux orphelins et aux veuves dans leur détresse, et à ne pas se laisser souiller par le monde.
fr.R: Voici la religion que Dieu le Père considère comme pure et bonne : prendre soin des orphelins et des veuves quand ils souffrent, et ne pas se laisser salir par le mal du monde.

ko.L: 하나님, 곧 아버지 앞에서 깨끗하고 더럽혀지지 않은 종교는 이것입니다. 곧 환난 가운데 있는 고아들과 과부들을 돌보고, 자기를 세상으로부터 물들지 않게 지키는 것입니다.
ko.B: 하나님 아버지께서 보시기에 깨끗하고 흠 없는 신앙생활은 이런 것입니다. 곤경에 처한 고아와 과부를 찾아가 돕고, 자기를 지켜 세상에 물들지 않는 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님 아버지께서 깨끗하고 좋다고 여기시는 신앙생활은 이런 것입니다. 고통당하는 고아와 과부를 돌보고, 세상의 악에 물들지 않게 자신을 지키는 것입니다.

vi.L: Sự sùng đạo trong sạch và không ô uế trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời [chúng ta], là Cha, là thế này: thăm viếng trẻ mồ côi và người góa bụa trong cơn hoạn nạn của họ, [và] giữ mình không bị thế gian làm hoen ố.
vi.B: Đối với Đức Chúa Trời là Cha, sự sùng đạo trong sạch và không tì vết là như thế này: đến giúp đỡ trẻ mồ côi và người góa bụa trong cơn khốn khó của họ, và giữ mình khỏi bị thế gian làm vấy bẩn.
vi.R: Đây là cách giữ đạo mà Đức Chúa Trời là Cha coi là trong sạch và tốt đẹp: chăm sóc trẻ mồ côi và người góa bụa khi họ gặp khổ đau, và không để điều xấu xa của thế gian làm vấy bẩn mình.

decisions.choice: visit: come to help and care for
decisions.reason: ἐπισκέπτομαι means to visit with care and help, as for the sick and the prisoner in Matthew 25:36. It is also the word for God visiting his people to save them (Luke 1:68).

decisions.choice: orphans and widows: the most unprotected people in society
decisions.reason: With no father or husband to support them, they had no one to speak for them. God is called their defender (Deuteronomy 10:18; Psalm 68:6), and the prophets judged Israel by how it treated them (Isaiah 1:17).

decisions.choice: the world: human life organized without and against God
decisions.reason: κόσμος here is not the created world but the values and ways opposed to God, as in 4:4 ("friendship with the world is enmity with God").

decisions.choice: God and Father: one person
decisions.reason: One article covers both words: God, who is the Father, the Father of the lights in verse 17.

decisions.choice: pure, undefiled, unstained: words from worship and sacrifice
decisions.reason: Clean and unblemished were the marks of acceptable worship and sacrifice (Leviticus 22:20; 1 Peter 1:19). James says the cleanness God accepts is mercy to the helpless and a life kept clean.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "to keep oneself unstained from the world"
decisions.reason: At least one early papyrus reads a different verb, so that the believers protect the orphans and widows from the world. The SBLGNT follows the great majority of manuscripts. This description is from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: [our] God and Father
decisions.reason: English cannot keep the article here; Literal supplies [our], as the phrase is used elsewhere (Philippians 4:20).

decisions.choice: not letting the world's evil make you dirty
alternatives: keep oneself unstained from the world
decisions.reason: Readable explains the stain picture: the evil of the world (see the meaning decision on "world").

decisions.choice: delante del Dios y Padre
decisions.reason: Spanish can keep the one article over both words ("del Dios y Padre"), so Literal needs no supplied "[nuestro]" as the English does.

decisions.choice: ulimwengu
decisions.reason: "Dunia" is the earth; "ulimwengu" is also the world of people and its ways, which is the sense here (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: venir en aide (B); prendre soin (R); visiter (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means coming to help and care for someone (m1). French "visiter" keeps the Greek word at Literal; at Balanced and Readable a plain "rendre visite" would sound like a social call.

decisions.choice: "세상" for the world at every level (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "세상" is the style guide's word for the world; the meaning decision reads it here as human life organized without God, which Readable makes explicit with "세상의 악".

decisions.choice: "thế gian" for the world at every level, through the letter
decisions.reason: The world here is human life organised without and against God (m3). "Thế gian" is the key term of the Vietnamese John for this sense; "thế giới" is the physical world.
